    What happens when you bring a room full of curious people together and ask them to build something that could make their city better? 💡 We had a pretty sweet weekend 🧁, as our community came together at Volta for the Claude Hackathon, tackling real problems and turning ideas into working solutions. The creativity in the room was incredible. Teams collaborated, experimented, built, and shared ideas that showed just how much can happen when you give people the space and tools to create. A huge thank you to everyone who spent their Saturday building with us. The ideas were great, but seeing the community come together around them was even better. 🚀 That’s a wrap on the Claude Hackathon! Jitakshi S. Rishabh A.

    Now this is news worth sharing. 🗞️📚 From putting books into the hands of people across the country to making headlines himself, a huge congratulations to Alex Liot, Founder of Volta resident company Wordsworth Gifting, on being featured in The Globe and Mail. Alex and Wordsworth are putting a novel spin on corporate gifting, using books to help companies create gifts that feel more thoughtful, personal and memorable. It’s always exciting to see the founders in our community, and the unique ideas they’re building, get national attention.

    Alex Liot
    2d

    A top 3 career moment this weekend 🗞️🚨 I’ve helped sell millions of newspapers, but apart from my name on page 2 and the occupational promotion announcement, I’ve never been featured in one, certainly not a 1/2 page in the Globe and Mail! It’s so perfectly written by Lana Hall MFA, and those are the best photos I’ve ever had taken by Aaron McKenzie Fraser, honestly beyond expectation. I have some links with 20 complementary reads, I’ll post in the comments below, please let me know if you hit the paywall. (Friends who are Globe subscribers, please considering also post a link from your account, tks!) Having a genuinely unique, “novel”, innovation is a double edged sword. It takes a LONG time to refine the core truths you feel, into messages and value proposition that actually land. Equally however, it is exactly these “never seen before” aspects that eventually get you incremental attention. I’m increasingly asked for advice by new founders or recent grads and it’s always the same. Find something or some way that no one has even done before and double down on what makes it’s different. It’s rough advice to be the contrarian but has served me well personally. Thanks to everyone (you know who you are) who has been so amazing along the way, you were standing right there with me in that photoshoot, wouldn’t been here with you.
